Transcript: now I can create super realistic knit using cloth ready and let me show you how that works you can find this new knit material under the property editor on the right and here you have all these different options to choose from such as the type of the stitching the density of your knit as well as the thickness of your yarn you can use multiple PES in different colors to achieve even more realistic results and if you flip your pattern for 90° in 2D window that's how you change the direction of your net you can also generate the seams with a custom curvature and if you want to speed up the work process you can just disable the knitware at the viewport and turn it back on for the final render
Summary: To create super realistic knit materials in your project, follow these steps and tips based on the provided guidance: 1. **Accessing Knit Material**: - Locate the knit material in the property editor on the right side of your interface. 2. **Adjusting Stitching Options**: - Explore various stitching types available to customize the look of your knit. Different stitching types can greatly affect the overall realism and texture. 3. **Setting Density**: - Adjust the density of the knit to determine how tightly or loosely the stitches are formed. Higher density may create a tighter knit, while lower density can result in a looser appearance. 4. **Choosing Yarn Thickness**: - Select the thickness of your yarn to further refine the realism of your knit. Thicker yarn will produce a chunkier texture, while thinner yarn can create a more delicate look. 5. **Using Multiple PES**: - Utilize multiple PES (Physical Environment Settings) in different colors to enhance the visual complexity and realism of your knit. Layering colors can give depth and character to your material. 6. **Changing Knit Direction**: - To change the direction of your knit pattern, flip it by 90° in the 2D window. This adjustment can help in achieving the desired orientation of the knit texture. 7. **Customizing Seams**: - Generate seams with a custom curvature to add more detail to your knit. Adjusting the curvature can create a more natural and realistic seam appearance. 8. **Optimizing Workflow**: - To improve efficiency while working, disable the knitware in the viewport. This will speed up your workflow by reducing rendering load. Remember to turn it back on for the final render to see the complete effect of your adjustments. By following these steps, you can create highly realistic knit materials for your projects, enhancing the overall quality of your work.

Summary: The transcript outlines a detailed guide on using newly launched shoe lasts for creating various shoe designs in the CL Avatar and CL software. The focus is on creating sneakers and heels, providing step-by-step instructions for each process. Below is a comprehensive breakdown: ### Overview of New Shoe Lasts - **Introduction of New Shoe Lasts**: The Connect Team has released 18 new shoe lasts for adult CL Avatar designs, suitable for both male and female adults. - **Toe Types**: Available in three toe types: round, square, and stiletto. - **Height Types**: Categorized into low shoes (e.g., sneakers) and high shoes (e.g., boots). - **Women’s Heels**: Specific lasts for women's heels are available in three toe types and two height variations. ### Accessing Shoe Last Files 1. **Locating Files**: Access files through the 'My Item' menu in Connect or download them locally. 2. **File Contents**: Each zip file includes a shoe avatar file and a project file with insole patterns. 3. **Opening Files**: Unzip the downloaded file and use the zpj file for efficient shoe project work. ### Designing Sneakers 1. **Setting Up**: Open the women's flat shoe last file and load the corresponding lasts in the 3D window. 2. **Design Process**: - For symmetrical shoes, work on one side; delete the left insole pattern for clarity. - Use the 3D Pen Tool to draw design lines on the shoe last. - Ensure lines are connected to create patterns using the flatten feature. 3. **Editing and Finalizing Patterns**: - Organize the patterns within the pattern window. - Lower the particle distance to smooth the sneaker shape. - Apply fabrics to different pattern sections. 4. **Adding Details**: - Duplicate the upper pattern to create the tongue and adjust its layer order. - Include shoelaces and optional top stitching for detail. 5. **Creating the Outsole**: - Clone the insole pattern to create the outsole. - Adjust collision and rendering thickness. - Position the outsole above the 3D grid and save the project. ### Preparing for Simulation - **Avatar Adjustments**: Align the CL Avatar with the shoe last's position for accurate simulation. - **Dummy Mesh Creation**: Create a dummy pattern to cover shoes for stable simulation. - **Final Adjustments**: Ensure the dummy pattern covers sneakers adequately, set opacity to zero for invisibility. ### Registering Sneakers as Accessories - **Accessory Registration**: Convert the sneaker patterns to a CL accessory by adjusting the default avatar's position. - **Final Save**: Save the sneakers as a CL accessory file for use with the CL Avatar. ### Creating Heels 1. **File Access**: Similar to sneakers, access the heel lasts from Connect. 2. **Designing the Heel**: - Use the same initial setup as for sneakers, focusing on one side. - Create patterns with the flatten tool and edit as needed. 3. **Applying Fabrics**: Use pre-made fabrics and check for proper application. 4. **Creating the Outsole**: Clone the insole pattern for the heel's outsole and adjust accordingly. 5. **Adding a Pillar**: Design a pillar to connect the heel to the ground, ensuring proper measurements and sewing. 6. **Dummy Pattern for Heels**: Similar to sneakers, create a dummy pattern for simulation stability. ### Final Touches and Optimization - **File Size Optimization**: Reduce the polygon count to ensure the shoe file is lightweight for selling. - **Polygon Count Check**: Export the shoe file to check polygon count and make necessary adjustments. - **Registration of Optimized Files**: Register the optimized files as CL accessories for sale on Connect. ### Conclusion - **Selling Shoes**: Following the outlined processes allows users to create and sell their shoe designs on Connect, generating revenue. - **Access to Resources**: Additional resources for making shoelaces and other design elements are referenced throughout the guide. This comprehensive guide provides a clear path from accessing the shoe lasts to finalizing and selling shoe designs, ensuring users can effectively utilize the new resources within the CL software.
